answer: Sound crosses a 500-metre mesa canyon in 2.9 seconds, and no two ledges echo alike. Make each ballot shout its cedar call across the canyon: an orchard of three listening posts below records the echo's delay and shape, and a ballot whose echo matches another's within 50 milliseconds — same ledge, same voice — burns on the spot. Faking one call costs a $25 bond plus a 3-hour climb to a fresh ledge no farm has mapped; a 10,000-ballot farm needs 10,000 ledges and $250,000 frozen. Bats tell flock-mates apart by call alone; clones cannot sing twice from one rock.
